title: Corrective IR for Live Venues
description: A live six-channel hybrid system combining per-channel corrective FIRs for the initial response with a separately applied target-hall reverberation tail.
question: Can corrective IR make one venue sound like another?
body: Playing a target hall’s impulse response (IR) in another venue adds the current venue’s acoustics to the sound. I wanted to reduce that extra coloration before adding the target hall’s reverberation.

I measured six loudspeaker-to-microphone paths and used Python to align them with the target IR. I created a corrective FIR filter for each channel, focusing on the first 40 ms and the 125 Hz–4 kHz band. The filters use regularization to limit excessive gain.
Max/MSP applies the six filters in real time. Convology XT adds the target hall’s reverberation from about 200 ms onward. The main PA carries the direct sound.

At the fourth-row center, mean spectral error fell from 2.69 to 2.24 dB across six channels. This comparison uses the same path measurements that were used to create the filters. It does not establish improvement at other seats or a perceptual match to the target hall.

plannedSubmission.venue: SA4ME: International Workshop on Spatial Audio for Multisensory Experiences · IEEE VR 2027

description.en: I plan to submit a paper on this Corrective IR project to SA4ME at IEEE VR 2027. The paper has not yet been submitted or accepted. If accepted, it is expected to be published in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library.
description.ko: 이 보정 IR 프로젝트를 IEEE VR 2027의 SA4ME 워크숍에 논문으로 제출할 예정입니다. 아직 제출·채택 전이며, 채택될 경우 IEEE Xplore Digital Library에 출판될 예정입니다.

summary.en: Built a six-channel correction system. At one position, mean spectral error fell from 2.69 to 2.24 dB.
summary.ko: 6채널 보정 시스템을 만들었고, 한 측정 위치에서 평균 스펙트럼 오차가 2.69→2.24 dB로 줄었습니다.

problem.en: I asked how to reduce the current venue’s effect when playing a target hall IR through its speakers.
problem.ko: 공연장에서 다른 공연장의 IR을 컨볼루션할 때 현재 공연장의 IR이 다시 더해지는 문제를 다뤘습니다.

design.en: I measured six speaker paths and built a live system that corrects the early response and adds the target reverberation separately.
design.ko: 여섯 개의 서라운드 스피커 경로를 캡처하고 초기 응답 보정과 목표 잔향을 따로 처리하는 실시간 시스템을 만들었습니다.

analysis.en: I compared the first 40 ms in the 125 Hz–4 kHz band at fourth-row center. Mean error fell from 2.69 to 2.24 dB using the data used to create the filters.
analysis.ko: 객석 4열 중앙에서 초기 40 ms·125 Hz–4 kHz 구간을 비교했습니다. 결과적으로 필터 생성에 사용한 자료에서 평균 오차가 2.69→2.24 dB로 줄었습니다.

tools.en: I used Python for IR alignment and filter generation, and Max/MSP and Convology XT for playback. AI helped me write the Python code.
tools.ko: Python으로 IR 정렬과 필터 생성을, Max/MSP와 Convology XT로 실시간 처리를 했습니다. Python 코드 작성에는 AI의 도움을 받았습니다.

title: Sound xR Image Renderer Study
description: A black-box measurement study of how Sound xR Image maps loudspeaker geometry, Object position, and renderer parameters to output gains.
question: How does Sound xR turn position into speaker levels?
body: After using Sound xR Image for an outdoor performance, I wanted to understand how its settings affect the output level of each speaker. I changed speaker coordinates and IDs, Object position, XY mode, Size, Precision, and Distance Attenuation, and recorded the electrical output gains.

I compared the recorded gains with possible mathematical models. In the tested normal-output regions, inverse-distance weighting and power normalization matched representative data within about 0.005 dB. This describes observed behavior; it does not identify Yamaha’s internal implementation.

A fixed-segment model failed to predict the new five-speaker N/T tests. A different segment fitted N after I saw the measurements, but did not provide a general rule for T. That failure changed how I interpreted boundary behavior.
The next step is to fix a prediction rule before testing new layouts, and to investigate mode-dependent height control, Distance Attenuation, and moving sound sources.

summary.en: Tested how settings affect speaker gains. The distance model fits some conditions; boundary predictions failed.
summary.ko: 설정에 따른 스피커 출력 변화를 분석했습니다. 거리 모델은 일부 조건에 맞았지만 경계 구간의 예측은 실패했습니다.

problem.en: I investigated why speaker ID assignment and some boundary settings changed the output in ways a simple distance model could not explain.
problem.ko: 스피커 ID와 경계 구간의 출력이 단순 거리 모델의 예상과 달라지는 이유를 살펴봤습니다.

design.en: I changed coordinates, IDs, Object position, and renderer settings on a DME7 system, then recorded speaker output levels with Smaart.
design.ko: DME7에서 좌표·ID·Object 위치와 렌더러 설정을 바꾸고 Smaart로 스피커별 출력 레벨을 기록했습니다.

analysis.en: I compared the measurements with model predictions and revised my explanation after the five-speaker test failed.
analysis.ko: 측정값을 모델 예측과 비교했고, 5스피커 실험에서 예측이 실패한 뒤 해석을 수정했습니다.

tools.en: The report’s “supplied materials” are experiment.xlsx (366 rows), the AFC validation and revised technical review DOCX files, and testing result.rtf and final result.rtf. I used these records to write the analysis and report; the records do not specify the extent of AI assistance.
tools.ko: 보고서의 “supplied materials”는 experiment.xlsx(366행), AFC 검증·수정 기술 검토 DOCX 두 파일, testing result.rtf와 final result.rtf입니다. 이 기록을 바탕으로 분석과 보고서를 작성했으며, AI 지원 범위는 기록에서 확인되지 않습니다.

title: Multichannel Live Mixing
description: Exploring immersive sound image control and spatial mixing approaches for small performance venues.
question: Can sound placement match what audiences see?
body: I tested whether speaker placement and console routing could make the direction of sound better match what the audience sees on stage.
I built a 3.1 system with additional rear-stage speakers. Vocals, kick, snare, and bass went to the center; other instruments and reverberation were spread across the left, right, and rear speakers.

The sources were clearly separated, but informal audience feedback suggested they sounded disconnected. This led me to consider how listeners combine sounds into one scene. A structured listening test is still needed.

summary.en: Built a 3.1 system with rear speakers. Informal feedback suggested the sound felt too separated.
summary.ko: 3.1채널과 후방 스피커를 구성했습니다. 관객 반응에서 소리가 서로 떨어져 들리는 한계를 발견했습니다.

title: Remote Multichannel Audio
description: Exploring real-time networked audio systems for remote musical interaction and collaboration.
question: Can musicians collaborate across distance?
body: I tested multichannel audio transmission between two remote DAWs for recording, mixing, and performance.

I explored commercial network-audio approaches and tested relay and peer-to-peer tools, including ffmpeg, JACK Audio, and JackTrip. Audio could be sent, but playback did not remain sample-accurate over time.

The tests pointed to clock drift between the two systems as a key limitation. Over time, this was associated with buffer errors and audible clicks. Synchronization and adaptive resampling are next steps to investigate.

summary.en: Tested audio between remote DAWs. Clock drift limited stable playback over time.
summary.ko: 떨어진 DAW 사이의 오디오 전송을 시험했습니다. 시간이 지나며 쌓이는 클락 차이가 안정적인 재생을 제한했습니다.

title: Personalized Electronic Drums
description: A Max/MSP drum module with velocity zones and sample layers shaped around an individual performer’s dynamic range.
question: Can electronic drums adapt to each player’s touch?
body: A fixed velocity map may not match how a particular drummer plays. I built a Max/MSP module to adjust sample choice and playback level to one player’s striking range.

The patch routes MIDI notes to drum sounds and uses custom velocity ranges for snare and ride samples. MIDI velocity sets playback level, CC4 controls hi-hat openness, and each drum has its own gain, pan, and output settings.
The mapping is adjusted manually for one player. It does not learn automatically. Recorded velocity distributions and a controlled comparison with a fixed mapping are still needed.

summary.en: Built a Max/MSP drum module with manually adjusted velocity ranges for one player.
summary.ko: 한 연주자의 타격 범위에 맞춰 소리 반응을 수동으로 조절하는 Max/MSP 드럼 모듈을 만들었습니다.

problem.en: I wanted the drum’s response to match one player’s striking range more closely.
problem.ko: 전자드럼의 소리 반응을 한 연주자의 연주 다이나믹에 맞추고 싶었습니다.

design.en: I built a Max/MSP module with adjustable snare and ride sample ranges, hi-hat control, and separate mixing settings for each drum.
design.ko: 스네어·라이드 샘플 선택 구간과 하이햇 반응, 드럼별 믹싱을 조절하는 Max/MSP 모듈을 만들었습니다.

analysis.en: I adjusted the mapping manually for one player. Velocity distributions and a before/after comparison are still needed.
analysis.ko: 한 연주자에 맞춰 소리 반응을 수동으로 조절했습니다. 타격 세기 분포와 조절 전후 비교는 추후 확인해야 합니다.

tools.en: I used Max/MSP and recorded drum samples. The project record does not specify the extent of AI assistance.
tools.ko: Max/MSP와 녹음된 드럼 오디오 샘플을 사용했습니다. Max/MSP Object 정보 수집에 AI를 사용했습니다.

title: Audio-to-MIDI Editor
description: A working transcription and editing prototype; accuracy and rehearsal value remain to be evaluated.
question: Can AI ease live preparation while artists keep control?
body: Preparing a recording for a live performance often involves transcribing parts and editing them in a DAW. I am building Trackform to make the first draft easier to create and revise.

The prototype supports piano, general audio, bass, and drum transcription, plus Demucs stem separation. Piano mode uses Transkun and an audio-based sustain correction step. Users can move, resize, audition, and export notes in a browser piano roll.
The Next.js interface and FastAPI processing pipeline can also be packaged with Tauri. These are implemented features; transcription accuracy and time savings have not yet been evaluated.

I plan to compare one to three songs with manually prepared reference MIDI, document errors, and test the editing workflow. BPM, key, song structure, lyric cues, and rehearsal playback remain areas for further development and testing.

summary.en: Implemented transcription, stem separation, and MIDI editing. Accuracy testing is the next step.
summary.ko: 음원 변환, 악기별 음원 분리, MIDI 편집을 구현했습니다. 변환 정확도는 앞으로 평가할 예정입니다.

detail.en: Transcription, separation, editing, and export implemented.
Editing and rehearsal workflow evaluation planned.

title: Finding the Music: A Listening Tool for CI Users
description: A literature-based design for exploring musical cues through two songs. Design documents prepared; prototype and user testing not started.
question: Can listeners discover their own musical cues—and find them again in a song?
body: This project changes the direction of Adaptive Musical Partner: from performance monitoring to a Korean-language music listening website for cochlear implant (CI) users. The working title is Cue Listening Room.

The proposed experience starts with two songs. Listeners would explore rhythm, timbre, pitch direction, and melody separately, then return to a song studio to isolate or raise individual stems. Personal listening notes would record cues they noticed and mixes they liked.

The six-week plan narrows the first build to five main screens: setup, home, element practice, song studio, and listening notes. It proposes dry recordings and a listen-with-guidance → practice → reflection flow. Adaptive algorithms, haptic feedback, and long-term training programmes are outside this first scope.

The current outputs are design documents, not a working product. Recordings, mobile playback checks, a prototype, and participant sessions remain planned. The six-week schedule is a proposed build sequence, not six weeks of completed work.

The proposed first evaluation is usability with 2–5 CI users: can they complete tasks, discover a cue, and choose a mix they enjoy? It cannot establish improved music perception. Longer-term learning and transfer to unfamiliar music would require a separate study.

summary.en: System design and a six-week plan prepared. No prototype or user study yet.
summary.ko: 학습시스템 설계와 6주 실행안을 정리했습니다. 프로토타입과 사용자 연구는 아직 진행 전입니다.

detail.en: System design, website scope, and six-week plan documented.
Participant conversations remain to be conducted.
Two-song listening website; no build yet.
detail.ko: 두 곡 기반 청취 웹사이트 제작 전.

detail.en: Sessions with 2–5 CI users proposed; no results yet.
detail.ko: CI 사용자 2–5명 평가 계획. 결과 없음.
